keySource: The key is NYSED's own, read from the Map to the Standards in the released-items PDF and carried into provenance/itemmap_g8-2026.json by tools/extract_item_map.py. tools/merge_content.py re-checks every letter against that file item by item and refuses to build if one disagrees, so the key in this spec cannot drift from the official table or be shifted by one released item. It was additionally checked against the transcribed choices: nine of the 34 are decided by reading the mathematics rather than the prose -- item 7's Pythagorean equation, item 15's product of powers, item 3's quotient of powers -- and in every case the keyed letter is the one the transcription makes true.

40.source: NYSED exemplary response, scoring materials page 12 (PDF page 8)
40.check: One third times pi times 3.2 squared times 12 = 128.68..., which rounds to 128.7. The radius and height are the ones in this item's own transcribed stem, so the answer and the transcription corroborate each other.

41.source: NYSED exemplary response, scoring materials page 17 (PDF page 13)
41.check: C is (-9,3) in the transcribed vertex list and the scale factor is one third about the origin, so C' is (-3,1). The vertex list is the part of this stem that was being cut in half before the extractor's right-hand bound was fixed, so the exemplary response is what confirms the repair.

43.source: NYSED exemplary response, scoring materials page 22 (PDF page 18)
43.check: (16^5)^4 is 16^20 and 16^8 times 16^12 is also 16^20, so the two sides are equal. Both exponents come from this item's own displayed expression, which decodes as (16^5)^4 O 16^8 . 16^12 -- an expression that was dropped entirely until the comparison circle was labelled.

44.source: NYSED exemplary response, scoring materials page 32 (PDF page 28)
44.check: B and D are the horizontal segments of the graph: distance is not changing while time is, so Sean is resting. The segment letters are read from this item's own figure, which is published as an image with a long description naming them.

45.source: NYSED exemplary response, scoring materials page 42 (PDF page 38)
45.check: 20.5 times 13.5 is 276.75, times 10 is 2,767.5. All three dimensions are in this item's transcribed stem.

46.source: NYSED exemplary response, scoring materials page 52 (PDF page 48)
46.check: y = -2.3(60) + 187 = -138 + 187 = 49. Both the equation and the 60 degrees F come from this item's own transcribed stem -- and the degree sign is one of the glyphs this test needed labelled, so the answer confirms the reading.

47.source: NYSED exemplary response, scoring materials page 62 (PDF page 58)
47.check: A circumference of 5.5 pi gives a diameter of 5.5 and a radius of 2.75, so the area is pi times 2.75 squared = 23.758..., which rounds to 24. The 5.5 pi is from this item's own stem.

48.source: NYSED exemplary response, scoring materials page 72 (PDF page 68)
48.check: Splash Zone charges 33.75 / 3 = $11.25 per person and Tube Time's graph has slope 12, so eight friends cost $90.00 and $96.00 -- a difference of $6.00. The $33.75 and the 3 are read from this item's own table image, described in its long description.
